es.B: Después de esto, Job abrió la boca y maldijo el día en que nació.
es.R: Después de esto, Job comenzó a hablar. Maldijo el día en que había nacido.

fr.B: Après cela, Job ouvrit la bouche et maudit le jour où il était né.
fr.R: Après cela, Job a commencé à parler. Il a maudit le jour de sa naissance.

sw.B: Baada ya hayo Ayubu alifungua kinywa chake, akailaani siku aliyozaliwa.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Ayubu alianza kusema. Aliilaani siku aliyozaliwa.

vi.L: Sau việc ấy, Gióp mở miệng và nguyền rủa ngày của mình.
vi.B: Sau đó, Gióp mở miệng nguyền rủa ngày mình được sinh ra.
vi.R: Sau đó, Gióp bắt đầu lên tiếng. Ông nguyền rủa ngày mình ra đời.

ko.L: 그 후에 욥이 자기 입을 열어 자기 날을 저주하였다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 욥이 입을 열어 자기가 태어난 날을 저주했다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 욥이 말을 꺼냈다. 그는 자기가 태어난 날을 저주했다.

pt.L: Depois disso, Jó abriu a boca e amaldiçoou o seu dia.
pt.B: Depois disso, Jó abriu a boca e amaldiçoou o dia em que tinha nascido.
pt.R: Depois disso, Jó começou a falar. Ele amaldiçoou o dia em que tinha nascido.

decisions.choice: opened his mouth: began to speak, after a long silence
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the start of a weighty speech. The three friends had sat with Job for seven days and nights without a word (2:13); Job is the first to break the silence, and his speech opens the poetry that runs to 42:6.

decisions.choice: cursed: real cursing, aimed at his day, not at God
decisions.reason: The verb (qalal, in the form meaning to call down evil on) is the plain word for cursing. In the prologue the Accuser said Job would curse God (1:11; 2:5), and his wife told him to do it (2:9); there the text uses "bless" as a cover word. Job does curse, but he curses his own day, not God.

decisions.choice: his day: the day of his birth
decisions.reason: Verse 3 says which day is meant: "the day I was born". "His day" can mean a person's birthday or a feast held on it (1:4).

decisions.choice: the day he was born
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which day is meant, as verse 3 does (m3); Literal keeps "his day".

decisions.choice: Passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable, in the narrative lines and speech introductions; the speeches themselves in present, future and passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The poetry of 3:2-42:6 is speech, and French does not use the passé simple in speech; only the narrator's lines keep the narrative tenses set in chapter 1.

vi.R: Ông nói:

ko.B: 욥이 말문을 열어 말했다.
ko.R: 그가 말했다.

pt.L: E Jó respondeu e disse:
pt.B: E Jó tomou a palavra e disse:
pt.R: Ele disse:

decisions.choice: answered: began to speak in response to what had happened
decisions.reason: No one has spoken to Job since 2:10. In Hebrew narrative "answered and said" can open a speech that responds to a situation, not to words (Deuteronomy 21:7; Judges 18:14). This line, like the other speech introductions in Job (4:1; 6:1; 8:1), stays prose.

decisions.choice: spoke up (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: "Answered" would make a reader look for a question no one asked (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew pair "answered and said".

decisions.choice: Speech introductions: "Y respondió X y dijo:" (L), "Entonces X respondió:" (B), "Entonces X dijo:" (R); here Balanced "tomó la palabra" and Readable "Dijo:", as the English
decisions.reason: The book's set formula for each speech; at this first one no one has spoken to Job, so Balanced and Readable avoid "respondió", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Speech introductions: "Et X répondit et dit :" (L), "Alors X répondit :" (B), "Alors X a dit :" (R); here Balanced "prit la parole" and Readable "Il a dit :", as the English
decisions.reason: The book's set formula for each speech; at this first one no one has spoken to Job, so Balanced and Readable avoid "répondit", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Speech introductions: "Ndipo X akajibu, akasema:" (L), "Kisha X akajibu:" (B), "Kisha X akasema:" (R); here Balanced "akaanza kunena" and Readable "Akasema:", as the English
decisions.reason: The book's set formula for each speech; at this first one no one has spoken to Job, so Balanced and Readable avoid "akajibu", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Speech introductions: "X đáp lời và nói:" (L), "Bấy giờ X đáp:" (B), "X nói:" (R); here Balanced "lên tiếng nói" and Readable "Ông nói:", as the English
decisions.reason: The book's set formula for each speech; at this first one no one has spoken to Job, so Balanced and Readable avoid "đáp", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Speech introductions: "그러자 X가 대답하여 말했다." (L), "그러자 X가 대답했다." (B), "그러자 X가 말했다." (R), ending with a period; here Balanced "말문을 열어 말했다" and Readable "그가 말했다", as the English
decisions.reason: The book's set formula for each speech; at this first one no one has spoken to Job, so Balanced and Readable avoid "대답했다", as the English does.

decisions.choice: speech introductions in prose, without quotation marks around the speech that follows
decisions.reason: For the whole book. The introductions stay prose with no line break, and the speeches that follow (3:3-42:6) are set as poetry with no quotation marks around them, as in the English; words quoted inside a speech take straight single quotes, as the English has them (3:3). The usual formula follows the English level by level: "E Elifaz, o temanita, respondeu e disse:" (L), "Então Elifaz, o temanita, respondeu:" (B), "Então Elifaz, o temanita, disse:" (R), with the speaker's full name; here the English has its own wording, and Portuguese follows it.

source.text: יֹ֣אבַד י֭וֹםאִוָּ֣לֶד בּ֑וֹ וְהַלַּ֥יְלָה אָ֝מַ֗ר הֹ֣רָה גָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Let perish [the] day I was born in it, and the night [which] said, Has been conceived a man.

en.L: Let the day perish on which I was born, \q and the night [that] said, 'A man has been conceived.'
en.B: Let the day I was born perish, \q and the night that said, 'A boy has been conceived!'
en.R: May the day I was born be wiped out, \q and the night that said, 'A boy has been conceived!'

es.L: Perezca el día en que nací, \q y la noche [que] dijo: “Un varón ha sido concebido”.
es.B: Que desaparezca el día de mi nacimiento, \q y la noche que anunció: “¡Un niño ha sido concebido!”.
es.R: Que el día en que nací sea borrado, \q y también la noche que dijo: “¡Se ha concebido un niño!”.

fr.L: Que périsse le jour où je suis né, \q et la nuit [qui] a dit : “Un homme a été conçu.”
fr.B: Qu’il périsse, le jour de ma naissance, \q et la nuit qui a annoncé : “C’est un garçon qui est conçu !”
fr.R: Que le jour où je suis né soit effacé, \q et la nuit qui a annoncé : “Un petit garçon est conçu !”

sw.L: Iangamie siku niliyozaliwa, \q na usiku uliosema, 'Mwanamume amechukuliwa mimba.'
sw.B: Siku niliyozaliwa na ipotee, \q na usiku uliosema, 'Mtoto wa kiume amechukuliwa mimba!'
sw.R: Siku niliyozaliwa na ifutwe kabisa, \q pamoja na usiku uliosema, 'Mtoto wa kiume amechukuliwa mimba!'

vi.L: Nguyện ngày tôi được sinh ra bị tiêu diệt, \q và đêm [đã] nói: 'Một người nam đã được thụ thai.'
vi.B: Ước gì ngày tôi sinh ra bị tiêu mất, \q cùng đêm đã nói: 'Một bé trai đã được thụ thai!'
vi.R: Ước gì ngày tôi chào đời bị xóa đi, \q và cả đêm đã nói: 'Một bé trai đã được thụ thai!'

ko.L: 내가 태어난 날이 망하고, \q '한 사내가 잉태되었다.' 하던 그 밤도 [망하여라].
ko.B: 내가 난 날은 망하여라. \q '사내아이가 잉태되었다!' 하던 밤도 망하여라.
ko.R: 내가 태어난 날은 지워져 버려라. \q '아들이 생겼다!' 하던 그 밤도 지워져 버려라.

pt.L: Pereça o dia em que eu nasci, \q e a noite que disse: 'Um homem foi concebido.'
pt.B: Que desapareça o dia em que nasci, \q e a noite que disse: 'Foi concebido um menino!'
pt.R: Que seja apagado o dia em que nasci, \q e a noite que disse: 'Foi concebido um menino!'

decisions.choice: Let it perish: a wish that the day had never been
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for wishes and curses. Job cannot undo his birth, so his curse wishes the day and night away from the calendar (verse 6). Jeremiah curses the day of his birth in the same way (Jeremiah 20:14-18).

decisions.choice: the night that said: the night is pictured as a person announcing the news
alternatives: the night in which it was said
decisions.reason: The night itself speaks, as if it were the first to know that a child had been conceived. The order runs backward, from the day of birth to the night of conception, as Job reaches for the very start of his life. Verses 4-5 take up the day and verses 6-10 the night.

decisions.choice: a man: a male child, named with the word for a grown man
decisions.reason: The word (gever) normally means a grown man in his strength. Used of a child just conceived, it looks ahead to the man he would become and to all that has now happened to him. It is used again of Job in verse 23. Because a particular male is meant, no inclusive wording is used.

decisions.choice: A boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "a boy", since "a man has been conceived" sounds odd in English; Literal keeps "a man" to show the Hebrew word (m3).

decisions.choice: May ... be wiped out
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain verb for the wish that the day had never been (m1).

decisions.choice: Job speaks of himself as "tôi" through the speeches
decisions.reason: Job is a man speaking among friends of equal standing; "tôi" is the neutral first person, used through his speeches to the friends (with "con" only when he speaks to God).

decisions.choice: Plain 해라체 for Job's lament; in the dialogues 하오체 (그대/그대들) only for lines addressed to the listener, plain 해라체 for descriptive passages and laments about oneself, and 합쇼체 with "주님"/"저" when Job speaks to God
decisions.reason: In chapter 3 Job addresses no one: he curses his day aloud, so the whole speech is in the plain style. The same rule holds through the book: a speech level marks a hearer, and passages that describe or lament take the plain written style of Korean poetry.

decisions.choice: lines set where each English level breaks them; present-tense wishes with "que"
alternatives: lines placed independently of the English
decisions.reason: For the whole book: each Portuguese level keeps exactly the \q line breaks of the same English level, so that the poetry has the same lines in every language; the words inside each line are arranged in Portuguese order. The wishes and curses take the present subjunctive ("Pereça", "que desapareça", "que seja apagado"), Portuguese's form for a wish. "Um homem" (L) shows the Hebrew word for a grown man (m3); Balanced and Readable say "um menino", as the English says "a boy".

source.text: הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֗וּא יְֽהִ֫י חֹ֥שֶׁךְ אַֽל־יִדְרְשֵׁ֣הוּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְאַל־תּוֹפַ֖ע עָלָ֣יו נְהָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The day that, let it be darkness; not let seek it God from above, and not let shine on it daylight.

en.L: That day, let it be darkness; \q let not God above seek it, \q and let no daylight shine on it.
en.B: That day, let it be darkness! \q May God above not look for it, \q and may no daylight shine on it.
en.R: Let that day turn into darkness. \q May God in heaven forget about it. \q May no light ever shine on it.

es.L: Aquel día, sea tinieblas; \q no lo busque Dios desde arriba, \q ni brille sobre él la claridad.
es.B: ¡Que ese día se vuelva tinieblas! \q Que Dios desde lo alto no se ocupe de él, \q y que no brille sobre él la luz del día.
es.R: Que ese día se convierta en oscuridad. \q Que Dios en el cielo se olvide de él. \q Que nunca brille luz sobre él.

fr.L: Ce jour-là, qu’il soit ténèbres ! \q Que Dieu d’en haut ne le recherche pas, \q et que nulle clarté ne brille sur lui !
fr.B: Ce jour-là, qu’il devienne ténèbres ! \q Que Dieu, là-haut, ne s’en soucie pas, \q et que la lumière du jour ne brille pas sur lui !
fr.R: Que ce jour se change en ténèbres. \q Que Dieu, dans le ciel, l’oublie. \q Qu’aucune lumière ne brille jamais sur lui.

sw.L: Siku ile, na iwe giza; \q Mungu aliye juu asiitafute, \q wala mwanga usiiangazie.
sw.B: Siku ile na iwe giza! \q Mungu aliye juu asiijali, \q wala nuru ya mchana isiiangazie.
sw.R: Siku ile na igeuke kuwa giza. \q Mungu aliye mbinguni na aisahau. \q Mwanga wowote usiiangazie kamwe.

vi.L: Ngày ấy, nguyện nó là tối tăm; \q nguyện Đức Chúa Trời ở trên cao đừng tìm đến nó, \q và ánh sáng chớ chiếu trên nó.
vi.B: Ngày ấy, nguyện nó hóa ra tối tăm! \q Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời trên cao chẳng đoái đến nó, \q và ánh sáng ban ngày chẳng soi trên nó.
vi.R: Ước gì ngày ấy biến thành bóng tối. \q Ước gì Đức Chúa Trời trên trời quên nó đi. \q Ước gì chẳng bao giờ có ánh sáng chiếu trên nó.

ko.L: 그날은 어둠이 되어라. \q 위에 계신 하나님께서 그날을 찾지 마시고, \q 빛도 그 위에 비치지 마라.
ko.B: 그날은 어둠이 되어 버려라. \q 위에 계신 하나님께서 그날을 돌아보지 않으시고, \q 햇빛도 그 위에 비치지 마라.
ko.R: 그날은 캄캄한 어둠이 되어라. \q 하늘에 계신 하나님께서 그날을 잊어 주시고, \q 어떤 빛도 그 위에 비치지 마라.

pt.L: Aquele dia, seja trevas; \q que Deus lá de cima não o procure, \q e que não brilhe sobre ele a luz do dia.
pt.B: Que aquele dia seja trevas! \q Que Deus lá do alto não pergunte por ele, \q e que nenhuma claridade brilhe sobre ele.
pt.R: Que aquele dia vire escuridão. \q Que Deus no céu se esqueça dele. \q Que nunca brilhe luz nenhuma sobre ele.

decisions.choice: let it be darkness: the reverse of God's first word in creation
decisions.reason: God's first words in creation are "Let there be light" (Genesis 1:3). Job uses the same form, "let it be", with "darkness" in place of "light". Through this curse he calls on the order of creation to be undone for his one day.

decisions.choice: seek: look for, take notice of, care for
decisions.reason: The verb (darash) means to seek out or look after; the land of Israel is one that "the LORD your God looks after" (Deuteronomy 11:12). Job wishes that God would never ask after his day, leaving it forgotten.

decisions.choice: God: the name Eloah
decisions.reason: Eloah is a form of the word for God used mostly in poetry, and more in Job than in any other book. It is rendered "God".

decisions.choice: May God in heaven forget about it
alternatives: Let not God above seek it
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what it would mean for God not to look for the day (m2), and "in heaven" for "from above".

decisions.choice: Deus for Eloah, El and Elohim
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Job's poetic names for God, Eloah (m3) and El, are "Deus" like Elohim, as the English says "God"; Shaddai is "o Todo-Poderoso" (5:17), and only YHWH takes the divine name setting.

source.text: יִגְאָלֻ֡הוּ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְ֭צַלְמָוֶת תִּשְׁכָּן־עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנָ֑ה יְ֝בַעֲתֻ֗הוּ כִּֽמְרִ֥ירֵי יֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let claim it darkness and deep darkness; let settle over it a cloud; let terrify it [the] blacknesses of [the] day.

en.L: Let darkness and deep darkness claim it; \q let a cloud settle over it; \q let the blackness of the day terrify it.
en.B: May darkness and deep gloom claim it as their own; \q may a cloud settle over it; \q may all that blackens the day terrify it.
en.R: May darkness and deep shadow take it back. \q May a cloud cover it. \q May everything that turns the day black fill it with terror.

es.L: Reclámenlo las tinieblas y la densa oscuridad; \q pósese sobre él una nube; \q atérrenlo las negruras del día.
es.B: Que las tinieblas y la densa oscuridad lo reclamen como suyo; \q que una nube se pose sobre él; \q que todo lo que ennegrece el día lo aterre.
es.R: Que la oscuridad y la sombra profunda lo recuperen. \q Que una nube lo cubra. \q Que todo lo que vuelve negro el día lo llene de terror.

fr.L: Que les ténèbres et l’ombre épaisse le réclament ; \q qu’une nuée s’installe sur lui ; \q que les noirceurs du jour l’épouvantent !
fr.B: Que les ténèbres et l’obscurité profonde le réclament comme leur bien ; \q qu’un nuage se pose sur lui ; \q que tout ce qui noircit le jour le remplisse d’effroi !
fr.R: Que les ténèbres et l’ombre profonde le reprennent. \q Qu’un nuage le recouvre. \q Que tout ce qui rend le jour noir le remplisse de terreur.

sw.L: Giza na giza nene na viidai; \q wingu na lifanye makao juu yake; \q weusi wa mchana na uitishe.
sw.B: Giza na giza nene na viidai kuwa mali yao; \q wingu na litulie juu yake; \q kila kitu kinachotia giza mchana na kiitishe.
sw.R: Giza na kivuli kizito na viichukue tena. \q Wingu na liifunike. \q Kila kitu kinachogeuza mchana kuwa giza na kiijaze hofu.

vi.L: Nguyện tối tăm và bóng tối dày đặc chiếm lấy nó; \q nguyện mây phủ trên nó; \q nguyện những gì làm đen ban ngày khiến nó kinh hãi.
vi.B: Nguyện tối tăm và bóng tối mịt mù đòi nó về làm của mình; \q nguyện một đám mây đậu trên nó; \q nguyện mọi điều làm đen tối ban ngày khiến nó kinh hoàng.
vi.R: Ước gì bóng tối và bóng đen dày đặc lấy nó lại. \q Ước gì mây che phủ nó. \q Ước gì mọi thứ làm ngày hóa đen khiến nó đầy kinh hãi.

ko.L: 어둠과 깊은 어둠이 그날을 되찾고, \q 구름이 그 위에 머물고, \q 낮을 검게 하는 것들이 그날을 두렵게 하여라.
ko.B: 어둠과 짙은 그늘이 그날을 제 것으로 되찾고, \q 구름이 그 위에 내려앉고, \q 낮을 캄캄하게 하는 모든 것이 그날을 떨게 하여라.
ko.R: 어둠과 짙은 그림자가 그날을 도로 가져가거라. \q 구름이 그날을 덮어라. \q 낮을 까맣게 만드는 모든 것이 그날을 무섭게 하여라.

pt.L: Que as trevas e a escuridão profunda o reivindiquem; \q que uma nuvem pouse sobre ele; \q que os negrumes do dia o aterrorizem.
pt.B: Que as trevas e a escuridão profunda o reivindiquem como seu; \q que uma nuvem se assente sobre ele; \q que tudo o que escurece o dia o encha de pavor.
pt.R: Que as trevas e a sombra mais escura o tomem de volta. \q Que uma nuvem o cubra. \q Que tudo o que deixa o dia escuro o encha de terror.

decisions.choice: claim: take back as one's own
decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is the one used of a relative who buys back family land or claims a family member (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4-6). Darkness, which was there before light (Genesis 1:2), is to come and claim the day as its own. A second verb spelled the same means "defile" (Malachi 1:7), but the first sense fits the picture better.

decisions.choice: deep darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) sounds like "shadow of death" and was long read that way (Psalm 23:4). It is most likely formed from a word for darkness and means the deepest darkness; Job uses it often of the darkness of the grave (10:21-22). The sound of death in it may be heard as well.

decisions.choice: the blackness of the day: whatever darkens daylight, such as an eclipse or a storm
decisions.reason: The word (kimrirey) is found only here. It is most likely formed from a root meaning to be black, and so speaks of what turns day to night. Others take it from the word for "bitter", giving "the bitter things of the day".

decisions.choice: claim it as their own
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "as their own" so that the picture of a relative claiming what belongs to the family is heard (m1).

decisions.choice: a escuridão profunda (L, B); a sombra mais escura (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (tsalmavet, also 10:21-22; 12:22; 16:16; 24:17; 28:3; 34:22; 38:17): the word most likely means the deepest darkness (m2), as the English "deep darkness" says; "sombra da morte" is the old reading of its sound, which the meaning note explains. "Reivindicar" is used for the claiming verb (m1) because "reclamar" means "complain" in Brazil.

source.text: הַלַּ֥יְלָה הַהוּא֮ יִקָּחֵ֪ה֫וּ אֹ֥פֶל אַל־יִ֭חַדְּ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר יְ֝רָחִ֗ים אַל־יָבֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: The night that, let take it gloom; not let it rejoice among [the] days of [the] year; in [the] number of [the] months not let it come.

en.L: That night, let gloom seize it; \q let it not rejoice among the days of the year; \q into the number of the months let it not come.
en.B: That night, let thick darkness carry it off; \q let it not rejoice among the days of the year \q or come into the count of the months.
en.R: Let deep darkness carry that night away. \q Do not let it celebrate with the other days of the year. \q Do not let it be counted in any month.

es.L: Aquella noche, apodérese de ella la oscuridad; \q no se alegre entre los días del año; \q en el número de los meses no entre.
es.B: Aquella noche, que se la lleve la densa oscuridad; \q que no se alegre entre los días del año \q ni entre en la cuenta de los meses.
es.R: Que la oscuridad profunda se lleve esa noche. \q Que no celebre con los demás días del año. \q Que no se cuente en ningún mes.

fr.L: Cette nuit-là, que l’obscurité la saisisse ; \q qu’elle ne se réjouisse pas parmi les jours de l’année ; \q dans le compte des mois, qu’elle n’entre pas !
fr.B: Cette nuit-là, que l’obscurité l’emporte ; \q qu’elle ne se réjouisse pas parmi les jours de l’année \q et n’entre pas dans le compte des mois.
fr.R: Que l’obscurité emporte cette nuit. \q Qu’elle ne fasse pas la fête avec les autres jours de l’année. \q Qu’elle ne soit comptée dans aucun mois.

sw.L: Usiku ule, utusitusi na uushike; \q usifurahi kati ya siku za mwaka; \q katika hesabu ya miezi usiingie.
sw.B: Usiku ule, giza nene na liuchukue; \q usifurahi pamoja na siku za mwaka, \q wala usiingie katika hesabu ya miezi.
sw.R: Giza nene na liuchukue usiku ule. \q Usisherehekee pamoja na siku nyingine za mwaka. \q Usihesabiwe katika mwezi wowote.

vi.L: Đêm ấy, nguyện bóng tối dày đặc bắt lấy nó; \q nguyện nó chẳng được vui giữa các ngày trong năm; \q nguyện nó chẳng vào trong số các tháng.
vi.B: Đêm ấy, nguyện bóng tối mịt mùng cuốn nó đi; \q nguyện nó chẳng được vui cùng các ngày trong năm \q cũng chẳng được kể vào số các tháng.
vi.R: Ước gì bóng tối dày đặc cuốn đêm ấy đi. \q Đừng cho nó vui mừng cùng những ngày khác trong năm. \q Đừng cho nó được tính vào tháng nào cả.

ko.L: 그 밤은 흑암이 붙잡아 가고, \q 한 해의 날들 가운데서 기뻐하지 못하며, \q 달들의 수에 들지 마라.
ko.B: 그 밤은 짙은 어둠이 휩쓸어 가거라. \q 한 해의 날들 가운데서 기뻐하지 못하고, \q 달의 수에도 들지 마라.
ko.R: 짙은 어둠이 그 밤을 쓸어 가 버려라. \q 그 밤은 한 해의 다른 날들과 함께 즐거워하지 마라. \q 어느 달에도 끼지 마라.

pt.L: Aquela noite, que a escuridão a arrebate; \q que ela não se alegre entre os dias do ano; \q que não entre no número dos meses.
pt.B: Aquela noite, que a escuridão densa a leve embora; \q que ela não se alegre entre os dias do ano \q nem entre na conta dos meses.
pt.R: Que a escuridão profunda leve embora aquela noite. \q Que ela não festeje com os outros dias do ano. \q Que não seja contada em nenhum mês.

decisions.choice: rejoice: take part in the joy of the year's days
alternatives: be joined to, be counted among
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew is pointed, the verb is from chadah, "rejoice": the night is not to share in the feasts and gladness of the year. The same letters could also be read as a form of yachad, "be joined", which would match "come into the number of the months" in the next line. Either way, Job wants the night struck from the calendar.

decisions.choice: gloom: thick darkness
decisions.reason: The word ('ofel) is a poetic word for deep darkness (10:22; 23:17). Darkness is to seize the night like a robber and carry it off, as the verb "take" often means.

decisions.choice: carry it off
decisions.reason: The verb is "take"; Balanced says "carry it off" because darkness takes the night away so that it is lost from the year (m2).

decisions.choice: celebrate with the other days
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common verb for sharing in the year's feasts (m1).

source.text: הִנֵּ֤ה הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַ֭הוּא יְהִ֣י גַלְמ֑וּד אַל־תָּבֹ֖א רְנָנָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, the night that, let it be barren; not let come a cry of joy in it.

en.L: Look, that night, let it be barren; \q let no cry of joy come into it.
en.B: Yes, let that night be barren; \q let no cry of joy be heard in it.
en.R: Let that night be empty, with no child conceived. \q Let no one shout for joy in it.

es.L: He aquí, aquella noche, sea estéril; \q no entre en ella grito de júbilo.
es.B: Sí, que esa noche sea estéril; \q que no se oiga en ella ningún grito de alegría.
es.R: Que esa noche quede vacía, sin que se conciba ningún niño. \q Que nadie grite de alegría en ella.

fr.L: Voici, cette nuit-là, qu’elle soit stérile ; \q qu’aucun cri de joie n’y entre !
fr.B: Oui, que cette nuit soit stérile ; \q qu’on n’y entende aucun cri de joie !
fr.R: Que cette nuit soit vide, sans aucun enfant conçu. \q Que personne n’y pousse un cri de joie.

sw.L: Tazama, usiku ule, na uwe tasa; \q kelele za furaha zisiingie ndani yake.
sw.B: Naam, usiku ule na uwe tasa; \q kelele za furaha zisisikike ndani yake.
sw.R: Usiku ule na uwe mtupu, bila mtoto kutungwa mimba. \q Mtu yeyote asipige kelele za furaha ndani yake.

vi.L: Kìa, đêm ấy, nguyện nó hiếm muộn; \q nguyện chẳng có tiếng reo vui nào vào trong nó.
vi.B: Phải, nguyện đêm ấy hiếm muộn; \q nguyện chẳng nghe tiếng reo vui nào trong nó.
vi.R: Ước gì đêm ấy trống rỗng, không có đứa trẻ nào được thụ thai. \q Ước gì không ai reo vui trong đêm ấy.

ko.L: 보라, 그 밤은 아무것도 낳지 못하는 밤이 되고, \q 기쁨의 외침이 그 안에 들어오지 마라.
ko.B: 그렇다, 그 밤은 아무것도 잉태하지 못하는 밤이 되고, \q 그 안에서 기뻐 외치는 소리가 들리지 마라.
ko.R: 그 밤은 텅 비어서 아무 아이도 생기지 마라. \q 아무도 그 밤에 기뻐 소리치지 마라.

pt.L: Eis que aquela noite, seja ela estéril; \q que não entre nela grito de alegria.
pt.B: Sim, que aquela noite seja estéril; \q que nela não se ouça nenhum grito de alegria.
pt.R: Que aquela noite fique vazia, sem nenhuma criança concebida. \q Que ninguém grite de alegria nela.

decisions.choice: barren: empty and lifeless, with no child conceived
decisions.reason: The word (galmud) is used of a woman with no children (Isaiah 49:21) and of a company that bears no life (15:34). Job wishes that nothing had been conceived on that night, that is, himself (verse 3).

decisions.choice: a cry of joy: the glad shout at the news of a coming child
decisions.reason: The birth of a son was greeted with gladness (Jeremiah 20:15; Ruth 4:13-17). Job wishes that night had brought no such joy.

decisions.choice: Yes
decisions.reason: The word (hinneh) points to what is said next and here adds weight. Literal keeps "Look"; Balanced uses "Yes" for the emphasis. Readable leaves it unsaid.

decisions.choice: empty, with no child conceived
decisions.reason: Readable says what "barren" means in this line (m1), since the word may be unclear to young readers.

source.text: יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ אֹרְרֵי־י֑וֹם הָ֝עֲתִידִ֗ים עֹרֵ֥ר לִוְיָתָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Let curse it [those who] curse [the] day, those ready to rouse Leviathan.

en.L: Let those who curse the day curse it, \q those ready to rouse Leviathan.
en.B: Let those who lay curses on days curse it, \q those who are skilled to rouse Leviathan.
en.R: Let the people who put curses on days curse that night, \q the ones who dare to wake Leviathan, the monster of the sea.

es.L: Maldíganla los que maldicen el día, \q los que están dispuestos a despertar a Leviatán.
es.B: Que la maldigan los que echan maldiciones sobre los días, \q los que saben despertar a Leviatán.
es.R: Que maldigan esa noche los que echan maldiciones sobre los días, \q los que se atreven a despertar a Leviatán, el monstruo del mar.

fr.L: Que ceux qui maudissent le jour la maudissent, \q ceux qui sont prêts à réveiller Léviathan !
fr.B: Que ceux qui jettent des malédictions sur les jours la maudissent, \q eux qui savent réveiller Léviathan !
fr.R: Que les gens qui jettent des sorts sur les jours maudissent cette nuit, \q ceux qui osent réveiller Léviathan, le monstre de la mer.

sw.L: Na waulaani wale walaanio siku, \q walio tayari kumwamsha Lewiathani.
sw.B: Wale wanaoweka laana juu ya siku na waulaani, \q wale walio stadi kumwamsha Lewiathani.
sw.R: Watu wanaoweka laana juu ya siku na waulaani usiku ule, \q wale wanaothubutu kumwamsha Lewiathani, joka kubwa la baharini.

vi.L: Nguyện những kẻ rủa ngày nguyền rủa nó, \q là những kẻ sẵn sàng khuấy động Lê-vi-a-than.
vi.B: Nguyện những kẻ chuyên trù ẻo ngày nguyền rủa nó, \q là những kẻ thạo việc đánh thức Lê-vi-a-than.
vi.R: Ước gì những người hay nguyền rủa ngày nguyền rủa đêm ấy, \q là những người dám đánh thức Lê-vi-a-than, con quái vật dưới biển.

ko.L: 날을 저주하는 자들이 그 밤을 저주하여라, \q 리워야단을 깨울 채비를 한 자들이.
ko.B: 날에 저주를 퍼붓는 자들이 그 밤을 저주하여라, \q 리워야단을 깨우는 데 능한 자들이.
ko.R: 날을 저주하는 사람들이 그 밤을 저주하여라. \q 바다 괴물 리워야단을 감히 깨우는 사람들이 그렇게 하여라.

pt.L: Que a amaldiçoem os que amaldiçoam o dia, \q os que estão prontos para despertar Leviatã.
pt.B: Que a amaldiçoem os que lançam maldições sobre os dias, \q os que têm a habilidade de despertar Leviatã.
pt.R: Que as pessoas que lançam maldições sobre os dias amaldiçoem aquela noite, \q as que têm coragem de acordar Leviatã, o monstro do mar.

decisions.choice: those who curse the day: people thought able to put a curse on a day
decisions.reason: In the ancient world some were believed to have power to lay curses that would make a day unlucky or bring disaster, as Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel (Numbers 22:6). Job calls on such people to curse his night. He calls on their skill; the text does not say he approves of it.

decisions.choice: Leviathan: a monster of the sea in Israel's poems
decisions.reason: Leviathan is the great sea creature of the old poems: a many-headed beast God crushed (Psalm 74:14), "the twisting serpent" (Isaiah 27:1), and also a creature God made to play in the sea (Psalm 104:26). Job 40:25-41:26 describes it at length as a beast no human can master. Here, those bold enough to rouse it could unleash a power that would swallow the day. The name is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: day, as the Hebrew is written
decisions.reason: The words for "day" and "sea" differ by one letter in Hebrew. "Those who curse the sea" would match Leviathan, the sea monster, in the next line, and the sea is linked with Leviathan elsewhere (Psalm 74:13-14). No Hebrew manuscript is known to read "sea"; this is a proposed reading. "Day" fits the whole curse of verses 3-10 and is kept. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: ready: prepared and skilled for a task
decisions.reason: The word ('atid) means prepared or ready (15:24; Esther 3:14). Here it speaks of people with the skill and daring to rouse a creature no one should wake (41:2).

decisions.choice: Leviathan, the monster of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and adds a short explanation of who Leviathan is (m2).

decisions.choice: "Leviatán" at every level; Readable adds "el monstruo del mar"
decisions.reason: The name of the sea monster of the old poems is kept (meaning decision m2); Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Léviathan" at every level; Readable adds "le monstre de la mer"
decisions.reason: The name of the sea monster of the old poems is kept (meaning decision m2); Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Lewiathani" at every level; Readable adds "joka kubwa la baharini"
decisions.reason: The name of the sea monster of the old poems is kept (meaning decision m2); Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Lê-vi-a-than" at every level; Readable adds "con quái vật dưới biển"
decisions.reason: The name of the sea monster of the old poems is kept (meaning decision m2); Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: "리워야단" at every level; Readable adds "바다 괴물"
decisions.reason: The name of the sea monster of the old poems is kept in its published Korean form (meaning decision m2); Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: Leviatã, as a name without the article; "Leviatã, o monstro do mar" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 40:25 and chapter 41): the Portuguese form of the name, written as a name, as the English writes "Leviathan"; Readable adds who he is, as the English Readable does (m2).

source.text: יֶחְשְׁכוּ֮ כּוֹכְבֵ֪י נִ֫שְׁפּ֥וֹ יְקַו־לְא֥וֹר וָאַ֑יִן וְאַל־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר׃

records.literal_gloss: Let grow dark [the] stars of its twilight; let it wait for light and [there be] none, and not let it see [the] eyelids of dawn.

en.L: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark; \q let it wait for light, and [there be] none, \q and let it not see the eyelids of the dawn.
en.B: Let the stars of its early dawn be dark; \q let it wait for light that never comes \q and never see the dawn open its eyes.
en.R: Let its morning stars stay dark. \q Let it wait for daylight that never comes. \q Do not let it see the first light of dawn.

es.L: Oscurézcanse las estrellas de su crepúsculo; \q espere la luz, y no [haya ninguna], \q y no vea los párpados de la aurora.
es.B: Que se oscurezcan las estrellas de su madrugada; \q que espere una luz que nunca llegue \q y nunca vea a la aurora abrir los ojos.
es.R: Que sus estrellas de la mañana se queden oscuras. \q Que espere la luz del día, y que nunca llegue. \q Que no vea la primera luz del amanecer.

fr.L: Que les étoiles de son crépuscule s’obscurcissent ; \q qu’elle attende la lumière, et [qu’il n’y en ait] pas, \q et qu’elle ne voie pas les paupières de l’aurore !
fr.B: Que les étoiles de son aube restent sombres ; \q qu’elle attende une lumière qui ne vienne jamais \q et ne voie jamais l’aurore ouvrir les yeux !
fr.R: Que ses étoiles du matin restent sombres. \q Qu’elle attende le jour, et qu’il ne vienne jamais. \q Qu’elle ne voie pas les premières lueurs de l’aube.

sw.L: Nyota za mapambazuko yake na zitiwe giza; \q na uingoje nuru, [isiwepo], \q wala usione kope za alfajiri.
sw.B: Nyota za alfajiri yake na zibaki gizani; \q na ungoje nuru isiyokuja kamwe, \q wala usione alfajiri ikifumbua macho yake.
sw.R: Nyota zake za asubuhi na zibaki gizani. \q Na ungoje mwanga wa mchana usiokuja kamwe. \q Usione mwanga wa kwanza wa alfajiri.

vi.L: Nguyện các ngôi sao lúc chạng vạng của nó trở nên tối tăm; \q nguyện nó trông đợi ánh sáng, mà [chẳng có], \q và chẳng thấy mí mắt của rạng đông.
vi.B: Nguyện các vì sao lúc tờ mờ sáng của nó cứ tối mịt; \q nguyện nó chờ ánh sáng mà ánh sáng chẳng bao giờ đến, \q và chẳng bao giờ thấy rạng đông mở mắt.
vi.R: Ước gì những ngôi sao buổi sớm của nó cứ tối đen. \q Ước gì nó chờ ánh ngày mà ánh ngày chẳng bao giờ đến. \q Đừng cho nó thấy tia sáng đầu tiên của bình minh.

ko.L: 그 밤의 새벽녘 별들이 어두워지고, \q 빛을 기다려도 [빛이] 없으며, \q 새벽의 눈꺼풀을 보지 못하여라.
ko.B: 그 밤의 새벽 별들이 어둠에 잠기고, \q 그 밤이 빛을 기다려도 끝내 오지 않으며, \q 새벽이 눈을 뜨는 것을 결코 보지 못하여라.
ko.R: 그 밤의 새벽 별들은 계속 어두워라. \q 날이 밝기를 기다려도 끝내 밝지 마라. \q 새벽의 첫 빛을 보지 못하여라.

pt.L: Que escureçam as estrelas do seu crepúsculo; \q que ela espere pela luz, e não [haja] nenhuma, \q e que não veja as pálpebras da aurora.
pt.B: Que as estrelas da sua madrugada fiquem escuras; \q que ela espere a luz que nunca chega \q e nunca veja a aurora abrir os olhos.
pt.R: Que as suas estrelas da manhã continuem apagadas. \q Que ela espere pela luz do dia, que nunca vem. \q Que ela não veja o primeiro clarão da aurora.

decisions.choice: its twilight: the half-light before dawn, when the morning stars still shine
decisions.reason: The word (neshef) is used of both evening and early morning twilight (7:4; Psalm 119:147). Since the night here waits for light and dawn, the twilight before daybreak is meant, when the stars of morning are seen (38:7).

decisions.choice: the eyelids of the dawn: the first rays of morning
decisions.reason: Dawn is pictured as opening its eyes as the first light spreads. Job uses the same picture of Leviathan's eyes in 41:10. Job asks that his night never reach morning.

decisions.choice: never see the dawn open its eyes
alternatives: see the eyelids of the dawn
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the dawn's eyes (m2) in a form English can follow; Readable says "the first light of dawn".

source.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א סָ֭גַר דַּלְתֵ֣י בִטְנִ֑י וַיַּסְתֵּ֥ר עָ֝מָ֗ל מֵעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For not it shut [the] doors of my womb, and hid trouble from my eyes.

en.L: For it did not shut the doors of my [mother's] womb \q and hide trouble from my eyes.
en.B: For it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb \q or hide trouble from my eyes.
en.R: For that night did not close my mother's womb \q and keep me from seeing all this trouble.

es.L: Porque no cerró las puertas del vientre [de mi madre] \q ni escondió de mis ojos la aflicción.
es.B: Porque no cerró las puertas del vientre de mi madre \q ni ocultó la desgracia de mis ojos.
es.R: Porque esa noche no cerró el vientre de mi madre \q para que yo no viera todo este sufrimiento.

fr.L: Car elle n’a pas fermé les portes du sein [de ma mère], \q et n’a pas caché le malheur à mes yeux.
fr.B: Car elle n’a pas fermé les portes du ventre de ma mère \q pour cacher la peine à mes yeux.
fr.R: Car cette nuit n’a pas fermé le ventre de ma mère \q pour m’empêcher de voir tout ce malheur.

sw.L: Kwa sababu haukuifunga milango ya tumbo [la mama yangu], \q wala haukuficha taabu machoni pangu.
sw.B: Kwa sababu haukuifunga milango ya tumbo la mama yangu \q wala kuificha taabu mbali na macho yangu.
sw.R: Kwa sababu usiku ule haukulifunga tumbo la mama yangu \q ili nisione taabu hii yote.

vi.L: Vì nó đã chẳng đóng các cửa của lòng [mẹ] tôi, \q và giấu sự khốn khổ khỏi mắt tôi.
vi.B: Vì nó đã chẳng đóng các cửa lòng mẹ tôi \q để giấu nỗi khốn khổ khỏi mắt tôi.
vi.R: Vì đêm ấy đã không đóng lòng mẹ tôi lại \q để tôi khỏi phải thấy tất cả nỗi khổ này.

ko.L: 그 밤이 내 [어머니의] 태의 문을 닫지 않았고, \q 고난을 내 눈에서 감추지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 밤이 내 어머니 태의 문을 닫지 않아서, \q 고통을 내 눈앞에서 가려 주지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그 밤이 내 어머니의 태를 닫아 버리지 않아서, \q 나는 이 모든 고통을 보게 되었다.

pt.L: Porque não fechou as portas do ventre [da minha mãe] \q e não escondeu dos meus olhos o sofrimento.
pt.B: Pois ela não fechou as portas do ventre da minha mãe \q nem escondeu o sofrimento dos meus olhos.
pt.R: Porque aquela noite não fechou o ventre da minha mãe \q para me poupar de ver todo este sofrimento.

decisions.choice: the doors of my womb: the womb I came from, my mother's womb
decisions.reason: "My womb" means the womb that held me. If the night had shut its doors, Job would never have been conceived or born. The same picture of doors at a birth is used of the sea in 38:8, and it is the LORD who closes or opens a womb (1 Samuel 1:5-6; Genesis 29:31).

decisions.choice: trouble: misery and painful toil
decisions.reason: The word ('amal) means both hard labor and the misery it brings. It runs through the book: Job calls himself one who suffers it (verse 20, from the same root) and Eliphaz answers that those who sow it reap it (4:8).

decisions.choice: my mother's womb (Literal: my [mother's] womb)
decisions.reason: English "my womb" would mean Job's own, so every level adds "mother's" (in brackets at Literal) to give the sense (m1).

source.text: לָ֤מָּה לֹּ֣א מֵרֶ֣חֶם אָמ֑וּת מִבֶּ֖טֶן יָצָ֣אתִי וְאֶגְוָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Why not from [the] womb did I die, [from the] belly came out and expire?

en.L: Why did I not die from the womb, \q come out from the belly and expire?
en.B: Why did I not die at birth, \q come out of the womb and breathe my last?
en.R: Why did I not die as soon as I was born? \q Why did I not breathe my last as I came out of my mother's body?

es.L: ¿Por qué no morí desde el seno, \q no salí del vientre y expiré?
es.B: ¿Por qué no morí al nacer, \q no salí del vientre y exhalé el último aliento?
es.R: ¿Por qué no me morí en cuanto nací? \q ¿Por qué no di mi último suspiro al salir del cuerpo de mi madre?

fr.L: Pourquoi ne suis-je pas mort dès le sein, \q ni n’ai expiré en sortant du ventre ?
fr.B: Pourquoi ne suis-je pas mort à la naissance, \q n’ai-je pas rendu le dernier souffle en sortant du ventre ?
fr.R: Pourquoi ne suis-je pas mort dès ma naissance ? \q Pourquoi n’ai-je pas rendu mon dernier souffle en sortant du ventre de ma mère ?

sw.L: Kwa nini sikufa tangu tumboni, \q nikatoka tumboni nikakata roho?
sw.B: Kwa nini sikufa wakati wa kuzaliwa, \q nikatoka tumboni na kukata roho?
sw.R: Kwa nini sikufa mara tu nilipozaliwa? \q Kwa nini sikukata roho nilipotoka tumboni mwa mama yangu?

vi.L: Sao tôi chẳng chết từ trong lòng mẹ, \q ra khỏi bụng mẹ mà tắt thở?
vi.B: Sao tôi chẳng chết ngay lúc mới sinh, \q vừa lọt lòng mẹ đã trút hơi thở cuối cùng?
vi.R: Sao tôi không chết ngay khi vừa sinh ra? \q Sao tôi không tắt thở khi vừa ra khỏi lòng mẹ?

ko.L: 어찌하여 나는 태에서 죽지 않았던가? \q 배에서 나와 숨을 거두지 않았던가?
ko.B: 어찌하여 나는 태어날 때 죽지 않았던가? \q 어머니 배에서 나오면서 숨을 거두지 않았던가?
ko.R: 왜 나는 태어나자마자 죽지 않았을까? \q 왜 어머니 몸에서 나올 때 숨이 끊어지지 않았을까?

pt.L: Por que desde o ventre não morri, \q [e] ao sair do seio não expirei?
pt.B: Por que não morri ao nascer? \q Por que não dei o último suspiro ao sair do ventre?
pt.R: Por que não morri logo que nasci? \q Por que não dei o último suspiro quando saí do corpo da minha mãe?

decisions.choice: from the womb: at birth, as soon as I was born
decisions.reason: "From the womb" often means "from birth" (Psalm 22:11; 58:4). The second line says the same: coming out of the belly and dying at once. Job does not ask for an answer; the questions of verses 11-23 are a lament, like Jeremiah 20:18.

decisions.choice: expire: breathe one's last, die
decisions.reason: The verb (gava') is the one used of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob breathing their last (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 49:33). Job uses it again of human death in 14:10.

decisions.choice: at birth
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the phrase means (m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

source.text: מַ֭דּוּעַ קִדְּמ֣וּנִי בִרְכָּ֑יִם וּמַה־שָּׁ֝דַ֗יִם כִּ֣י אִינָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Why did receive me knees, and why breasts that I should suck?

en.L: Why did knees receive me, \q and why [were there] breasts, that I should nurse?
en.B: Why were there knees to receive me, \q and breasts for me to nurse at?
en.R: Why was there a lap to hold me \q and a breast to feed me?

es.L: ¿Por qué me recibieron unas rodillas, \q y por qué [había] pechos para que mamara?
es.B: ¿Por qué hubo rodillas que me recibieran, \q y pechos que me amamantaran?
es.R: ¿Por qué hubo un regazo que me sostuviera \q y un pecho que me alimentara?

fr.L: Pourquoi des genoux m’ont-ils reçu, \q et pourquoi [y avait-il] des seins pour que je tète ?
fr.B: Pourquoi y avait-il des genoux pour m’accueillir, \q et des seins pour m’allaiter ?
fr.R: Pourquoi m’a-t-on pris sur ses genoux \q et donné le sein pour me nourrir ?

sw.L: Kwa nini magoti yalinipokea, \q na kwa nini [kulikuwa na] matiti, ili ninyonye?
sw.B: Kwa nini kulikuwa na magoti ya kunipokea, \q na matiti ya kuninyonyesha?
sw.R: Kwa nini kulikuwa na mapaja ya kunibeba \q na titi la kunilisha?

vi.L: Sao có đầu gối đỡ lấy tôi, \q và sao [có] vú cho tôi bú?
vi.B: Sao lại có đầu gối để đón nhận tôi, \q và bầu sữa để tôi bú?
vi.R: Sao lại có lòng ai ẵm tôi \q và dòng sữa mẹ nuôi tôi?

ko.L: 어찌하여 무릎이 나를 받았으며, \q 어찌하여 내가 빨 젖이 [있었던가]?
ko.B: 어찌하여 나를 받아 줄 무릎이 있었고, \q 내가 빨 젖이 있었던가?
ko.R: 왜 나를 안아 줄 품이 있었고, \q 나를 먹일 젖이 있었을까?

pt.L: Por que me receberam os joelhos, \q e por que [havia] seios para que eu mamasse?
pt.B: Por que havia joelhos para me receber \q e seios para eu mamar?
pt.R: Por que havia um colo para me segurar \q e um peito para me alimentar?

decisions.choice: knees received me: the newborn was taken onto someone's knees and so welcomed into the family
decisions.reason: A newborn laid on the knees was received and cared for. It may be the mother's lap, or the father taking the child on his knees as his own (Genesis 50:23; compare 30:3). Either way, Job was welcomed and kept alive when he wishes he had not been.

decisions.choice: why breasts that I should nurse: why was I fed and kept alive
decisions.reason: The second question shortens the first: "why [were there] breasts". Without a lap and a mother's milk a newborn would not have lived.

decisions.choice: a lap
decisions.reason: Readable says "a lap", the place where a baby is held, since "knees received me" is not clear in English (m1).

source.text: כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה שָׁכַ֣בְתִּי וְאֶשְׁק֑וֹט יָ֝שַׁ֗נְתִּי אָ֤ז׀יָנ֬וּחַֽ לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept; then [there would be] rest to me,

en.L: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; \q I would have slept; then [there would be] rest for me,
en.B: For by now I would be lying at peace; \q I would be asleep and at rest,
en.R: If I had died then, I would be lying quietly now. \q I would be asleep and at rest.

es.L: Porque ahora estaría acostado y tranquilo; \q dormiría; entonces [habría] reposo para mí,
es.B: Porque ahora estaría descansando en paz; \q estaría dormido y en reposo,
es.R: Si hubiera muerto entonces, ahora estaría acostado en calma. \q Estaría dormido y descansando.

fr.L: Car maintenant je serais couché et tranquille ; \q je dormirais ; alors [il y aurait] du repos pour moi,
fr.B: Car à présent je serais étendu en paix ; \q je dormirais, je serais en repos,
fr.R: Si j’étais mort alors, je serais couché tranquillement maintenant. \q Je dormirais et je serais en repos.

sw.L: Kwa maana sasa ningekuwa nimelala na kutulia; \q ningekuwa nimelala usingizi; ndipo [ningekuwa na] raha,
sw.B: Kwa maana sasa ningekuwa nimelala kwa amani; \q ningekuwa usingizini na kupumzika,
sw.R: Kama ningekufa wakati ule, sasa ningekuwa nimelala kimya. \q Ningekuwa usingizini na kupumzika.

vi.L: Vì bây giờ tôi đã nằm yên và được bình lặng; \q tôi đã ngủ; bấy giờ [tôi đã] được nghỉ ngơi,
vi.B: Vì giờ đây tôi đã nằm yên bình; \q tôi đã ngủ và được an nghỉ,
vi.R: Nếu khi ấy tôi chết đi, thì giờ đây tôi đang nằm yên lặng. \q Tôi đang ngủ và được nghỉ ngơi.

ko.L: 그러면 지금쯤 나는 누워서 고요히 있을 것이고, \q 잠들어 있을 것이니, 그때에는 나에게 안식이 [있을] 텐데,
ko.B: 그랬다면 지금쯤 나는 평안히 누워 있고, \q 잠들어 쉬고 있을 텐데,
ko.R: 그때 죽었더라면 나는 지금 조용히 누워 있을 것이다. \q 잠들어 쉬고 있을 것이다.

pt.L: Pois agora eu estaria deitado e tranquilo; \q eu dormiria; então [haveria] descanso para mim,
pt.B: Pois agora eu estaria deitado em paz; \q estaria dormindo e descansando,
pt.R: Se eu tivesse morrido naquela hora, estaria agora deitado em silêncio. \q Estaria dormindo e descansando.

decisions.choice: now I would have lain down: what would be true if he had died at birth
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what would have been: had Job died at birth, he would now be at rest. The sentence runs on through verse 15.

decisions.choice: lain down, slept, rest: death pictured as sleep and rest
decisions.reason: Lying down and sleeping are common pictures of death (14:12; Psalm 13:4; Daniel 12:2). For Job, longing for an end to his pain, the grave would be quiet and rest, the very things he says in verse 26 that he does not have.

decisions.choice: If I had died then
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the "for now" assumes (m1), and ends the sentence here where Literal and Balanced run on into verse 14.

source.text: עִם־מְ֭לָכִים וְיֹ֣עֲצֵי אָ֑רֶץ הַבֹּנִ֖ים חֳרָב֣וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: with kings and counselors of [the] earth, who built ruins for themselves,

en.L: with kings and counselors of the earth, \q who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
en.B: with the kings and counselors of the earth, \q who rebuilt ruined places for themselves,
en.R: I would be with the kings and advisers of the earth, \q who built up ruined cities for themselves.

es.L: con reyes y consejeros de la tierra, \q que reedificaban ruinas para sí,
es.B: con los reyes y los consejeros de la tierra, \q que reconstruían lugares en ruinas para sí,
es.R: Estaría con los reyes y los consejeros de la tierra, \q que reconstruyeron para sí ciudades en ruinas.

fr.L: avec les rois et les conseillers de la terre, \q qui se rebâtissaient des ruines,
fr.B: avec les rois et les conseillers de la terre, \q qui relevaient pour eux-mêmes des lieux en ruine,
fr.R: Je serais avec les rois et les conseillers de la terre, \q qui reconstruisaient pour eux-mêmes des villes en ruine.

sw.L: pamoja na wafalme na washauri wa dunia, \q waliojijengea upya magofu,
sw.B: pamoja na wafalme na washauri wa dunia, \q waliojijengea upya mahali palipobomoka,
sw.R: Ningekuwa pamoja na wafalme na washauri wa dunia, \q waliojijengea upya miji iliyobomoka.

vi.L: với các vua và các mưu sĩ trên đất, \q là những người đã xây lại các nơi đổ nát cho mình,
vi.B: cùng với các vua và các mưu sĩ trên đất, \q là những người đã tái thiết các nơi hoang tàn cho mình,
vi.R: Tôi sẽ ở cùng các vua và các cố vấn trên đất, \q là những người đã xây lại các thành đổ nát cho mình.

ko.L: 땅의 왕들과 모사들과 함께, \q 곧 자기를 위하여 폐허를 다시 세운 자들과 함께,
ko.B: 세상의 왕들과 모사들, \q 곧 무너진 곳을 자기를 위해 다시 세운 이들과 함께,
ko.R: 나는 세상의 왕들과 그들의 고문들과 함께 있을 것이다. \q 그들은 무너진 성읍들을 자기를 위해 다시 세운 사람들이다.

pt.L: com reis e conselheiros da terra, \q que reconstruíram ruínas para si,
pt.B: com os reis e os conselheiros da terra, \q que reconstruíram para si lugares em ruínas,
pt.R: Eu estaria com os reis e os conselheiros da terra, \q que reconstruíram cidades em ruínas para si mesmos.

decisions.choice: who rebuilt ruins: who built up ruined places to make a name for themselves
alternatives: who built for themselves what are now ruins
decisions.reason: The words read "who build ruins for themselves". The sense is most likely that these kings rebuilt ruined cities, a boast of rulers (compare Isaiah 58:12; 61:4). It can also be taken with a twist: they built great buildings that are now ruins. Either way, all their building has not kept them from the grave, where Job would lie beside them.

decisions.choice: kings and counselors of the earth: the most powerful people of the world
decisions.reason: Kings and their counselors stood for power and wisdom. In death, Job would lie with them as an equal (verse 19).

decisions.choice: I would be with
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence, so it repeats the verb from verse 13.

source.text: א֣וֹ עִם־שָׂ֭רִים זָהָ֣ב לָהֶ֑ם הַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: or with princes, gold [was] to them, who filled their houses [with] silver.

en.L: or with princes [who had] gold, \q who filled their houses [with] silver.
en.B: or with officials who had gold, \q who filled their houses with silver.
en.R: I would be with leaders who had gold \q and filled their houses with silver.

es.L: o con príncipes [que tenían] oro, \q que llenaban sus casas [de] plata.
es.B: o con los jefes que tenían oro, \q que llenaban sus casas de plata.
es.R: Estaría con dirigentes que tenían oro \q y llenaban sus casas de plata.

fr.L: ou avec les princes [qui avaient] de l’or, \q qui remplissaient leurs maisons [d’]argent.
fr.B: ou avec les hauts fonctionnaires qui possédaient de l’or \q et qui remplissaient leurs maisons d’argent.
fr.R: Je serais avec les dirigeants qui avaient de l’or \q et qui remplissaient leurs maisons d’argent.

sw.L: au pamoja na wakuu [waliokuwa na] dhahabu, \q walioyajaza majumba yao [kwa] fedha.
sw.B: au pamoja na maafisa waliokuwa na dhahabu, \q walioyajaza majumba yao fedha.
sw.R: Ningekuwa pamoja na viongozi waliokuwa na dhahabu \q na kuyajaza majumba yao fedha.

vi.L: hoặc với các quan trưởng [có] vàng, \q là những người chất đầy bạc trong nhà mình.
vi.B: hoặc với các quan chức có nhiều vàng, \q đã chất đầy bạc trong nhà mình.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ ở cùng những người lãnh đạo có vàng \q và chứa đầy bạc trong nhà.

ko.L: 또는 금을 [가진] 고관들, \q 자기 집을 은으로 채운 자들과 함께 [있을 텐데].
ko.B: 또는 금을 가진 관리들, \q 자기 집을 은으로 가득 채운 이들과 함께 있을 텐데.
ko.R: 나는 금을 가진 지도자들과 함께 있을 것이다. \q 그들은 자기 집을 은으로 가득 채운 사람들이다.

pt.L: ou com príncipes [que tinham] ouro, \q que encheram de prata as suas casas.
pt.B: ou com altos oficiais que tinham ouro, \q que encheram de prata as suas casas.
pt.R: Estaria com líderes que tinham ouro \q e enchiam de prata as suas casas.

decisions.choice: princes rich in gold and silver: wealth that does not save from death
decisions.reason: The great of the earth are in the grave too, and their riches did not go down with them in any way that helped (Psalm 49:17-18). There, rich and poor are alike (verse 19).

decisions.choice: their houses: their homes, possibly also their tombs
decisions.reason: "Their houses" is most simply the palaces they filled with wealth. Since the verse speaks of the dead, some take the houses as their tombs, filled with silver buried with them; a tomb is called a house in 17:13 and 30:23.

decisions.choice: officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The word (sar) is "princes" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable, as elsewhere in these books.

source.text: א֤וֹכְנֵ֣פֶל טָ֭מוּן לֹ֣א אֶהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝עֹלְלִ֗ים לֹא־רָ֥אוּ אֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Or like a miscarriage hidden not was I, like infants [who] have not seen light?

en.L: Or [why] was I not like a hidden stillborn [child], \q like infants [who] never saw light?
en.B: Or why was I not like a stillborn child, hidden away, \q like infants who never see the light?
en.R: Why was I not like a baby born dead and buried out of sight, \q like babies who never see the light of day?

es.L: ¿O [por qué] no fui como un abortivo escondido, \q como niños [que] nunca vieron la luz?
es.B: ¿O por qué no fui como un niño nacido muerto, escondido, \q como los pequeños que nunca ven la luz?
es.R: ¿Por qué no fui como un bebé que nace muerto y es enterrado sin que nadie lo vea, \q como los bebés que nunca ven la luz del día?

fr.L: Ou [pourquoi] n’ai-je pas été comme un mort-né caché, \q comme des petits enfants [qui] n’ont jamais vu la lumière ?
fr.B: Ou pourquoi n’ai-je pas été comme un enfant mort-né qu’on enfouit, \q comme les petits qui ne voient jamais la lumière ?
fr.R: Pourquoi n’ai-je pas été comme un bébé mort à la naissance et enterré en cachette, \q comme ces bébés qui ne voient jamais la lumière du jour ?

sw.L: Au [kwa nini] sikuwa kama mimba iliyoharibika iliyofichwa, \q kama vitoto [ambavyo] havikuona nuru kamwe?
sw.B: Au kwa nini sikuwa kama mtoto aliyezaliwa amekufa, aliyefichwa, \q kama vitoto visivyoona nuru kamwe?
sw.R: Kwa nini sikuwa kama mtoto aliyezaliwa akiwa amekufa na kuzikwa mahali pasipoonekana, \q kama watoto wachanga wasioona kamwe mwanga wa mchana?

vi.L: Hoặc [sao] tôi chẳng như một thai sẩy bị giấu đi, \q như những trẻ thơ [chưa] hề thấy ánh sáng?
vi.B: Hoặc sao tôi chẳng như một đứa trẻ chết lúc sinh, bị chôn giấu đi, \q như những hài nhi chẳng bao giờ thấy ánh sáng?
vi.R: Sao tôi không như một đứa bé chết khi sinh ra và bị chôn khuất đi, \q như những em bé chẳng bao giờ thấy ánh mặt trời?

ko.L: 또는 [어찌하여] 나는 감추어진 낙태아처럼, \q 빛을 보지 못한 아기들처럼 되지 않았던가?
ko.B: 아니면 어찌하여 나는 몰래 묻힌 사산아처럼, \q 빛을 보지 못하는 아기들처럼 되지 못했던가?
ko.R: 왜 나는 죽은 채로 태어나 남몰래 묻힌 아기처럼, \q 햇빛을 한 번도 보지 못한 아기들처럼 되지 못했을까?

pt.L: Ou [por que] não fui como um natimorto escondido, \q como crianças [que] nunca viram a luz?
pt.B: Ou por que não fui como uma criança que nasce morta e é escondida, \q como os bebês que nunca veem a luz?
pt.R: Por que não fui como um bebê que nasce morto e é enterrado longe dos olhos de todos, \q como os bebês que nunca veem a luz do dia?

decisions.choice: Or [why] was I not: the verse takes up the questions of verses 11-12 again
alternatives: Or I would not have been (a wish)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "or like a hidden stillborn I was not". It goes back to the questions of verses 11-12 after the picture of rest in verses 13-15, and may also be heard as a wish that he had never been at all. Verses 17-19 then return to the place of the dead.

decisions.choice: a hidden stillborn child: a baby born dead and buried out of sight
decisions.reason: The word (nefel, from "fall") is a child born dead (Psalm 58:9; Ecclesiastes 6:3). "Hidden" means buried quietly and never known.

decisions.choice: seen light: been born and lived
decisions.reason: To see the light is to be born and live (verse 20; Psalm 49:20). A stillborn child never does.

decisions.choice: [why]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "why" in brackets so that the question of verses 11-12 can be followed (m1).

source.text: שָׁ֣ם רְ֭שָׁעִים חָ֣דְלוּ רֹ֑גֶז וְשָׁ֥ם יָ֝נ֗וּחוּ יְגִ֣יעֵי כֹֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: There [the] wicked cease [from] turmoil, and there rest [the] weary of strength.

en.L: There the wicked cease [from] turmoil, \q and there the weary of strength rest.
en.B: There the wicked stop their raging, \q and there those whose strength is spent are at rest.
en.R: In the grave, wicked people stop causing trouble, \q and those who are worn out can rest.

es.L: Allí los impíos dejan [de] perturbar, \q y allí reposan los agotados de fuerzas.
es.B: Allí los malvados dejan de enfurecerse, \q y allí descansan los que ya no tienen fuerzas.
es.R: En la tumba, los malvados dejan de causar problemas, \q y los que están agotados pueden descansar.

fr.L: Là, les méchants cessent [leur] agitation, \q et là les épuisés de force se reposent.
fr.B: Là, les méchants cessent leur fureur, \q et là ceux dont la force est à bout trouvent le repos.
fr.R: Dans la tombe, les méchants arrêtent de faire du mal, \q et ceux qui sont épuisés peuvent se reposer.

sw.L: Huko waovu hukoma ghasia zao, \q na huko waliochoka nguvu hupata pumziko.
sw.B: Huko waovu huacha kufanya fujo, \q na huko wale walioishiwa nguvu hupumzika.
sw.R: Kaburini waovu huacha kuleta taabu, \q na wale waliochoka sana hupata kupumzika.

vi.L: Ở đó kẻ ác thôi [gây] xáo động, \q và ở đó những người kiệt sức được nghỉ ngơi.
vi.B: Ở đó kẻ ác thôi cơn hung bạo, \q và ở đó những người đã cạn sức được an nghỉ.
vi.R: Trong mồ mả, kẻ ác không còn gây rối nữa, \q và những người mệt nhọc được nghỉ ngơi.

ko.L: 거기서는 악인들이 소란을 그치고, \q 거기서는 힘이 다한 자들이 쉰다.
ko.B: 거기서는 악인들도 날뛰기를 그치고, \q 거기서는 기력이 다한 사람들이 안식을 누린다.
ko.R: 무덤 속에서는 악한 사람들도 말썽을 그친다. \q 지친 사람들도 거기서 쉴 수 있다.

pt.L: Ali os perversos cessam [a] agitação, \q e ali repousam os exaustos de força.
pt.B: Ali os perversos param com a sua agitação, \q e ali descansam os que não têm mais forças.
pt.R: Na sepultura, os perversos param de causar problemas, \q e os que estão esgotados podem descansar.

decisions.choice: there: in the place of the dead
decisions.reason: "There" is the grave, where Job would lie with kings (verses 13-15). The book calls it Sheol (7:9; 14:13).

decisions.choice: turmoil: agitation, raging
decisions.reason: The word (rogez) means restless agitation. Here it is the raging of the wicked that troubles others; it can also be their own unrest. Job ends the chapter with the same word for what has come on him (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the weary of strength: those whose strength is worn out
decisions.reason: The phrase describes people exhausted by labor or suffering. In the grave they rest at last.

decisions.choice: In the grave
decisions.reason: Readable names the place "there" refers to (m1).

decisions.choice: o perverso, os perversos (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (26 times): the wicked (rasha') are "os perversos" at every level, the word most of the book uses (15:20; 21:7; 27:13; 36:6; 38:13), so the reader hears one word for the friends' stock figure of the wicked man and for Job's answer to it. "O ímpio" is kept for the godless (chanef, 8:13) and "o injusto" for 'awwal (18:21), so the three Hebrew words stay apart.

source.text: יַ֭חַד אֲסִירִ֣ים שַׁאֲנָ֑נוּ לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ ק֣וֹל נֹגֵֽשׂ׃

records.literal_gloss: Together prisoners are at ease; not they hear [the] voice of [the] taskmaster.

en.L: Together the prisoners are at ease; \q they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.
en.B: Prisoners are at ease together; \q they no longer hear the shout of the slave driver.
en.R: Prisoners rest there together. \q They no longer hear the shouts of the one who forced them to work.

es.L: Juntos los prisioneros están tranquilos; \q no oyen la voz del capataz.
es.B: Los presos están tranquilos todos juntos; \q ya no oyen los gritos del capataz de esclavos.
es.R: Allí los prisioneros descansan juntos. \q Ya no oyen los gritos del que los obligaba a trabajar.

fr.L: Ensemble les prisonniers sont tranquilles ; \q ils n’entendent pas la voix du chef de corvée.
fr.B: Les prisonniers y sont tranquilles ensemble ; \q ils n’entendent plus les cris du gardien d’esclaves.
fr.R: Les prisonniers s’y reposent ensemble. \q Ils n’entendent plus les cris de celui qui les forçait à travailler.

sw.L: Wafungwa hustarehe pamoja; \q hawaisikii sauti ya msimamizi wa kazi.
sw.B: Wafungwa hustarehe pamoja huko; \q hawasikii tena kelele za msimamizi wa watumwa.
sw.R: Wafungwa hupumzika huko pamoja. \q Hawasikii tena kelele za yule aliyewalazimisha kufanya kazi.

vi.L: Những kẻ bị tù cùng nhau được yên ổn; \q họ chẳng nghe tiếng của kẻ đốc công.
vi.B: Những tù nhân cùng được thảnh thơi; \q họ chẳng còn nghe tiếng quát của kẻ cai nô lệ.
vi.R: Ở đó các tù nhân cùng được nghỉ ngơi. \q Họ không còn nghe tiếng quát tháo của kẻ bắt họ làm việc.

ko.L: 갇힌 자들이 함께 평안히 있고, \q 감독관의 목소리를 듣지 않는다.
ko.B: 거기서는 갇힌 사람들이 다 함께 편히 쉬고, \q 노예 감독의 고함 소리를 더는 듣지 않는다.
ko.R: 갇혔던 사람들도 거기서는 함께 쉰다. \q 억지로 일을 시키던 자의 고함 소리를 더는 듣지 않는다.

pt.L: Juntos os prisioneiros estão tranquilos; \q não ouvem a voz do capataz.
pt.B: Os prisioneiros descansam juntos; \q já não ouvem os gritos do capataz.
pt.R: Ali os prisioneiros descansam juntos. \q Já não ouvem os gritos de quem os obrigava a trabalhar.

decisions.choice: the taskmaster: one who drives forced labor
decisions.reason: The word (nogesh) is the one used for the Egyptian slave drivers who forced Israel to work (Exodus 3:7; 5:6). Captives were often set to forced labor; in the grave they hear their driver no more.

decisions.choice: together: all alike, side by side
decisions.reason: The prisoners lie together in the place of the dead and all share the same ease.

decisions.choice: the shout of the slave driver
decisions.reason: The "voice" of a taskmaster is his shouted orders, and "slave driver" is the plain English for one who drives forced labor (m1).

source.text: קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חָפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Small and great there [is] he, and [the] slave [is] free from his master.

en.L: Small and great are there [alike], \q and the slave [is] free from his master.
en.B: Small and great are there alike, \q and slaves are free from their masters.
en.R: Ordinary people and important people are all there together. \q And slaves are free from their masters.

es.L: Pequeño y grande están allí [por igual], \q y el esclavo [está] libre de su amo.
es.B: Allí están por igual pequeños y grandes, \q y los esclavos quedan libres de sus amos.
es.R: La gente sencilla y la gente importante están todos allí juntos. \q Y los esclavos quedan libres de sus amos.

fr.L: Petit et grand sont là [pareils], \q et l’esclave [est] libre de son maître.
fr.B: Petits et grands y sont pareils, \q et les esclaves sont libérés de leurs maîtres.
fr.R: Les gens simples et les gens importants sont tous là ensemble. \q Et les esclaves sont libres de leurs maîtres.

sw.L: Mdogo na mkubwa wako huko [sawasawa], \q na mtumwa [yuko] huru mbali na bwana wake.
sw.B: Wadogo na wakubwa wako huko sawasawa, \q na watumwa wako huru mbali na mabwana zao.
sw.R: Watu wa kawaida na watu mashuhuri wote wako huko pamoja. \q Na watumwa wako huru mbali na mabwana zao.

vi.L: Kẻ nhỏ và người lớn đều ở đó [như nhau], \q và kẻ nô lệ [được] tự do khỏi chủ mình.
vi.B: Người hèn kẻ sang ở đó đều như nhau, \q và những người nô lệ được thoát khỏi chủ mình.
vi.R: Người thường và người quyền thế đều ở đó với nhau. \q Những người nô lệ cũng được tự do khỏi chủ mình.

ko.L: 작은 자와 큰 자가 거기 [똑같이] 있고, \q 노예가 그 주인에게서 자유롭다.
ko.B: 거기서는 작은 자나 큰 자나 똑같고, \q 노예들도 주인에게서 놓여 자유롭다.
ko.R: 평범한 사람도 높은 사람도 모두 거기 함께 있다. \q 노예들도 주인에게서 풀려나 자유롭다.

pt.L: O pequeno e o grande ali [são iguais], \q e o escravo [está] livre do seu senhor.
pt.B: Pequenos e grandes ali são iguais, \q e os escravos estão livres dos seus senhores.
pt.R: Gente simples e gente importante estão todas juntas ali. \q E os escravos estão livres dos seus donos.

decisions.choice: there [is] he: they are there alike, all the same
decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" after "small and great" sets them side by side: they are there, the same. Death makes no difference between them.

decisions.choice: the slave is free: an owned slave released from a master
decisions.reason: The word ('eved) here means a slave owned by a master, set against "free" (chofshi), the word used for a slave's release (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12). In the grave the slave is finally set free.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Where slave and free are set against each other, "slave" is kept at every level; "servant" would lose the point (m2).

decisions.choice: slaves ... their masters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since all slaves are meant, men and women; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: "노예" at every level
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Korean uses "종" for this word, but here slave is set against free, and "노예" keeps that contrast, as the English keeps "slave" at every level.

source.text: לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Why does he give to [the] sufferer light, and life to [the] bitter of soul,

en.L: Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give light to the sufferer, \q and life to the bitter of soul,
en.B: Why is light given to those in misery, \q and life to the bitter in soul,
en.R: Why does God give light to people who suffer? \q Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give life to those whose hearts are bitter?

es.L: ¿Por qué da {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} luz al que sufre, \q y vida a los amargados de alma,
es.B: ¿Por qué se da luz a los que sufren, \q y vida a los de alma amargada,
es.R: ¿Por qué Dios da luz a los que sufren? \q ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da vida a los que tienen el corazón amargado?

fr.L: Pourquoi donne-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la lumière au malheureux, \q et la vie à ceux qui ont l’âme amère,
fr.B: Pourquoi la lumière est-elle donnée à ceux qui souffrent, \q et la vie à ceux dont l’âme est amère,
fr.R: Pourquoi Dieu donne-t-il la lumière à ceux qui souffrent ? \q Pourquoi donne-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la vie à ceux qui ont le cœur plein d’amertume ?

sw.L: Kwa nini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} humpa mwenye taabu nuru, \q na uhai wale wenye uchungu rohoni,
sw.B: Kwa nini nuru hupewa wale walio katika taabu, \q na uhai wale wenye uchungu moyoni,
sw.R: Kwa nini Mungu huwapa nuru watu wanaoteseka? \q Kwa nini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huwapa uhai wale wenye uchungu moyoni?

vi.L: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban ánh sáng cho kẻ khốn khổ, \q và sự sống cho người có linh hồn cay đắng,
vi.B: Sao ánh sáng được ban cho người khốn khổ, \q và sự sống cho kẻ có tâm hồn cay đắng,
vi.R: Sao Đức Chúa Trời lại ban ánh sáng cho người đau khổ? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban sự sống cho người có lòng cay đắng?

ko.L: 어찌하여 그분은 고난받는 자에게 빛을 주시고, \q 영혼이 쓰라린 자에게 생명을 주시는가?
ko.B: 어찌하여 고난당하는 자에게 빛이 주어지고, \q 마음이 쓰라린 자에게 생명이 주어지는가?
ko.R: 왜 하나님께서는 고통받는 사람들에게 빛을 주시는가? \q 왜 그분은 마음이 쓰라린 사람들에게 생명을 주시는가?

pt.L: Por que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dá luz ao que sofre, \q e vida aos amargurados de alma,
pt.B: Por que é dada luz aos que estão na miséria, \q e vida aos que têm a alma amargurada,
pt.R: Por que Deus dá luz a quem sofre? \q Por que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dá vida aos que têm o coração amargo?

decisions.choice: he gives: the giver is not named, but it is God
decisions.reason: The verb is "he gives" with no subject. Job does not name God until verse 23, but he is the one who gives life and light (1:21). Literal keeps "he" and Readable names him; Balanced uses the passive, as the Hebrew leaves him unnamed.

decisions.choice: light and life: being alive
decisions.reason: "Light" stands for life itself, as in verse 16, "infants who never saw light". The two lines say the same thing twice.

decisions.choice: the bitter of soul: people in deep anguish
decisions.reason: Bitterness of soul is deep grief, as Hannah's was (1 Samuel 1:10) and that of the Shunammite whose son had died (2 Kings 4:27). The soul (nefesh) is the whole inner self.

decisions.choice: is light given
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the passive, keeping the giver unnamed as the Hebrew does (m1).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver (m1), so that the question is clear, and then uses a deity pronoun.

decisions.choice: Each Korean verse of 20-23 is a full sentence, ending in "?" or "."
alternatives: one sentence run on from verse 20 to 23
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb at the end, so a question running across four verses would leave verse 20 without its verb; each verse is closed and the next takes up the people described, keeping every verse's content after its own marker.

source.text: הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: those who wait for death, and it [is] not, and they dig for it more than [for] hidden treasures,

en.L: who wait for death, and it [does] not [come], \q and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
en.B: who long for death, but it does not come, \q and search for it more than for hidden treasure,
en.R: They long for death, but it does not come. \q They search for it harder than people dig for buried treasure.

es.L: que esperan la muerte, y no [llega], \q y cavan por ella más que por tesoros escondidos,
es.B: que anhelan la muerte, pero no llega, \q y la buscan más que a un tesoro escondido,
es.R: Desean la muerte, pero no llega. \q La buscan con más empeño que quien cava buscando un tesoro enterrado.

fr.L: qui attendent la mort, et elle [ne vient] pas, \q et la cherchent en creusant plus que des trésors cachés,
fr.B: qui aspirent à la mort, mais elle ne vient pas, \q et qui la recherchent plus qu’un trésor caché,
fr.R: Ils désirent la mort, mais elle ne vient pas. \q Ils la cherchent plus ardemment que ceux qui creusent pour trouver un trésor enfoui.

sw.L: wanaongojea kifo, nacho [hakiji], \q na kukichimbua kuliko hazina zilizofichwa,
sw.B: wanaotamani kifo lakini hakiji, \q na kukitafuta kuliko hazina iliyofichwa,
sw.R: Wanatamani kufa, lakini kifo hakiji. \q Wanakitafuta kwa bidii kuliko watu wanaochimba kutafuta hazina iliyofichwa.

vi.L: là những kẻ trông chờ sự chết, mà nó [chẳng đến], \q và đào tìm nó hơn tìm kho báu giấu kín,
vi.B: là những người mong chết mà cái chết chẳng đến, \q và tìm kiếm nó hơn tìm kho báu chôn giấu,
vi.R: Họ mong được chết, nhưng cái chết không đến. \q Họ tìm cái chết còn hơn người ta đào bới tìm kho báu.

ko.L: 그들은 죽음을 기다려도 [오지] 않고, \q 숨겨진 보물보다 더 그것을 파서 찾는다.
ko.B: 그들은 죽기를 바라도 죽음이 오지 않아, \q 숨겨진 보물을 찾기보다 더 애써 죽음을 찾는다.
ko.R: 그들은 죽기를 바라지만 죽음은 오지 않는다. \q 그들은 땅에 묻힌 보물을 찾는 사람보다 더 열심히 죽음을 찾는다.

pt.L: que esperam pela morte, e ela não [vem], \q e cavam por ela mais do que por tesouros escondidos,
pt.B: que anseiam pela morte, mas ela não vem, \q e a procuram mais do que a um tesouro escondido,
pt.R: Eles desejam a morte, mas ela não vem. \q Procuram por ela com mais esforço do que quem cava atrás de um tesouro enterrado.

decisions.choice: wait for: long for, wait eagerly
decisions.reason: The verb (chakah) is used of waiting with longing (Isaiah 30:18; Psalm 33:20). These people long for death as others long for good things.

decisions.choice: dig for it more than for hidden treasure: seek it with all their effort
decisions.reason: Buried treasure was sought with great effort (Proverbs 2:4; compare Job 28:1-11). Those in misery search for death harder than anyone digs for gold.

decisions.choice: [does] not [come]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "and it is not"; Literal supplies the verb in brackets.

source.text: הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי־גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ־קָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: the [ones] rejoicing to rejoicing; they exult when they find [the] grave,

en.L: who rejoice to [the point of] gladness, \q [who] exult when they find the grave,
en.B: who are filled with joy \q and glad when they find the grave,
en.R: They are full of joy \q when at last they find the grave.

es.L: que se alegran hasta [el] regocijo, \q [que] se gozan cuando hallan el sepulcro,
es.B: que se llenan de alegría \q y se gozan cuando encuentran el sepulcro,
es.R: Se llenan de alegría \q cuando por fin encuentran la tumba.

fr.L: qui se réjouissent jusqu’[à] l’allégresse, \q [qui] exultent quand ils trouvent le tombeau,
fr.B: qui sont remplis de joie \q et heureux quand ils trouvent le tombeau,
fr.R: Ils sont pleins de joie \q quand enfin ils trouvent le tombeau.

sw.L: wanaofurahi hata [kufikia] shangwe, \q [wanaoshangilia] wanapolipata kaburi,
sw.B: wanaojaa furaha \q na kushangilia wanapolipata kaburi,
sw.R: Wanajaa furaha \q wanapolipata kaburi hatimaye.

vi.L: là những kẻ vui mừng đến [độ] hân hoan, \q [và] hớn hở khi tìm được mồ mả,
vi.B: là những người tràn đầy niềm vui \q và hớn hở khi tìm được mồ mả,
vi.R: Họ vô cùng vui sướng \q khi cuối cùng tìm được mồ mả.

ko.L: 그들은 기뻐 뛰놀 만큼 즐거워하고, \q 무덤을 찾으면 크게 기뻐한다.
ko.B: 그들은 기쁨에 넘쳐서, \q 무덤을 찾으면 즐거워한다.
ko.R: 그들은 마침내 무덤을 찾게 되면 \q 기뻐서 어쩔 줄 모른다.

pt.L: que se alegram até o júbilo, \q [que] exultam quando acham a sepultura,
pt.B: que se enchem de alegria \q e ficam felizes quando encontram a sepultura,
pt.R: Eles ficam cheios de alegria \q quando finalmente encontram a sepultura.

decisions.choice: rejoicing to rejoicing: joy beyond measure
decisions.reason: "Rejoicing to rejoicing" builds the word on itself for emphasis: they are glad to the point of exultation. Some read the last word as gal, "heap" (of stones over a grave), with different vowels, which would fit "the grave" in the next line; the Hebrew as it is pointed reads "rejoicing".

decisions.choice: when they find the grave: the end of their search
decisions.reason: The word "find" completes the picture of verse 21: those who dig for death as for treasure are glad when at last they find it.

source.text: לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר־דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: to a man whose way is hidden, and [whom] has hedged God around him?

en.L: to a man whose way is hidden, \q and whom God has hedged in?
en.B: to a man whose way is hidden from him, \q whom God has fenced in?
en.R: Why give life to a man who cannot see where his life is going, \q whom God has shut in on every side?

es.L: al hombre cuyo camino está escondido, \q y a quien Dios ha cercado?
es.B: al hombre cuyo camino le está oculto, \q a quien Dios ha encerrado con un cerco?
es.R: ¿Por qué dar vida a un hombre que no ve hacia dónde va su vida, \q a quien Dios ha encerrado por todos lados?

fr.L: à l’homme dont le chemin est caché, \q et que Dieu a entouré d’une haie ?
fr.B: à l’homme dont le chemin lui est caché, \q que Dieu a enfermé derrière une haie ?
fr.R: Pourquoi donner la vie à un homme qui ne voit pas où va sa vie, \q que Dieu a enfermé de tous côtés ?

sw.L: kwa mtu ambaye njia yake imefichwa, \q na ambaye Mungu amemzungushia uzio?
sw.B: kwa mtu ambaye njia yake imefichika kwake, \q ambaye Mungu amemzungushia uzio?
sw.R: Kwa nini ampe uhai mtu asiyeona maisha yake yanaelekea wapi, \q ambaye Mungu amemfungia pande zote?

vi.L: cho người có đường lối bị che khuất, \q và bị Đức Chúa Trời rào quanh?
vi.B: cho người không thấy được đường lối mình, \q người mà Đức Chúa Trời đã rào kín?
vi.R: Sao lại ban sự sống cho người không thấy đời mình đi về đâu, \q người bị Đức Chúa Trời vây kín mọi bề?

ko.L: 길이 숨겨진 사람에게, \q 하나님께서 사방을 울타리로 막으신 사람에게 어찌하여 [생명을 주시는가]?
ko.B: 자기 앞길이 보이지 않는 사람, \q 하나님께서 울타리로 가두신 사람에게 어찌하여 생명을 주시는가?
ko.R: 왜 하나님께서는 자기 인생이 어디로 가는지 모르는 사람에게 생명을 주시는가? \q 왜 사방을 막아 가두신 사람에게 생명을 주시는가?

pt.L: a um homem cujo caminho está escondido, \q e a quem Deus cercou?
pt.B: a um homem cujo caminho lhe está escondido, \q a quem Deus cercou por todos os lados?
pt.R: Por que dar vida a um homem que não consegue ver para onde vai a sua vida, \q a quem Deus fechou por todos os lados?

decisions.choice: God has hedged him in: the hedge of 1:10, now felt as a prison
decisions.reason: The verb (sukh) is the one the Accuser used in 1:10: "Have you not put a hedge around him?" There the hedge was God's protection. Job now feels God's hedge as a wall that shuts him in with no way out (19:8).

decisions.choice: whose way is hidden: who cannot see where his life is going or why
decisions.reason: A person's way is the course of his life. Job cannot see the reason for what has happened or any way forward.

decisions.choice: to a man: Job speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The question that began in verse 20 ("why is light given ...") ends here. Job speaks of anyone in misery, but verses 24-26 show that he means himself; "a man" (gever) is the word used of him in verse 3. So no inclusive wording is used.

decisions.choice: Why give life to
decisions.reason: Readable broke verses 20-22 into short sentences, so it repeats the question here.

decisions.choice: hidden from him
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "from him" so that "hidden" is understood as he cannot see it (m2).

decisions.choice: "cercado"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word of 1:10 ("un cerco alrededor de él"), so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "entouré d'une haie" (L), "enfermé derrière une haie" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "haie" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "amemzungushia uzio" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "uzio" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "rào quanh" (L), "rào kín" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the verb "rào" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "울타리로 막으신" (L), "울타리로 가두신" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the "울타리" of 1:10, so the reader hears that the hedge that protected Job now shuts him in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Deus cercou
decisions.reason: "Cercar" is the verb of the hedge in 1:10 ("puseste uma cerca ao redor dele"), so Portuguese keeps the echo m1 describes: the protection is now felt as a wall.

source.text: כִּֽי־לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For before my bread my sighing comes, and pour out like water my groans.

en.L: For before my bread my sighing comes, \q and my groans pour out like water.
en.B: For sighing comes to me in place of food, \q and my groans pour out like water.
en.R: Instead of food, I have sighing. \q My groans pour out like water.

es.L: Porque delante de mi pan llega mi suspiro, \q y como agua se derraman mis gemidos.
es.B: Porque los suspiros me llegan en lugar de comida, \q y mis gemidos se derraman como el agua.
es.R: En vez de comida, tengo suspiros. \q Mis gemidos corren como el agua.

fr.L: Car avant mon pain vient mon soupir, \q et mes gémissements se répandent comme l’eau.
fr.B: Car les soupirs me tiennent lieu de nourriture, \q et mes plaintes déferlent comme l’eau.
fr.R: Au lieu de manger, je soupire. \q Mes gémissements coulent comme de l’eau.

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla ya mkate wangu kuugua kwangu huja, \q na kilio changu chamwagika kama maji.
sw.B: Kwa maana kuugua kunanijia badala ya chakula, \q na kilio changu kinamiminika kama maji.
sw.R: Badala ya chakula, nina kuugua. \q Kilio changu kinamwagika kama maji.

vi.L: Vì trước bánh tôi, tiếng thở than tôi đến, \q và tiếng rên rỉ tôi tuôn ra như nước.
vi.B: Vì tiếng thở than thay cho đồ ăn của tôi, \q và tiếng rên rỉ tôi tuôn trào như nước.
vi.R: Thay vì ăn, tôi chỉ thở than. \q Tiếng rên rỉ của tôi tuôn ra như nước.

ko.L: 내 빵 앞에 내 탄식이 오고, \q 내 신음은 물처럼 쏟아진다.
ko.B: 한숨이 밥 대신 나를 찾아오고, \q 신음이 물처럼 쏟아진다.
ko.R: 나는 먹는 대신 한숨만 쉰다. \q 내 신음 소리가 물처럼 쏟아진다.

pt.L: Pois antes do meu pão vem o meu suspiro, \q e os meus gemidos se derramam como água.
pt.B: Pois os suspiros me vêm no lugar da comida, \q e os meus gemidos se derramam como água.
pt.R: Em vez de comida, eu tenho suspiros. \q Os meus gemidos se derramam como água.

decisions.choice: before my bread: in place of food, as my daily food
decisions.reason: "Before my bread" can mean that sighing comes ahead of his food, or in place of it, as in "my tears have been my food day and night" (Psalm 42:4). Either way, grief fills his days.

decisions.choice: my groans: loud cries of pain
decisions.reason: The word (she'agah) is used of a lion's roar (4:10). Job's cries of pain are loud and pour out without stopping.

decisions.choice: in place of food (B); instead of food (R)
